To find the median of the data set presented in the stem-and-leaf plot, we need to convert each entry from minutes and seconds into seconds. The stem represents minutes, and the leaves represent seconds. Each entry is converted as follows:

- \(0 | 28\ 28\ 50\) converts to \(28, 28, 50\) seconds.
- \(1 | 00\ 02\) converts to \(60, 62\) seconds.
- \(2 | 20\ 25\ 35\ 43\ 45\) converts to \(140, 145, 155, 163, 165\) seconds.
- \(3 | 00\ 00\ 00\ 30\ 36\) converts to \(180, 180, 180, 210, 216\) seconds.
- \(4 | 00\ 00\) converts to \(240, 240\) seconds.

Listing all converted times in order, we get:
\[28, 28, 50, 60, 62, 140, 145, 155, 163, 165, 180, 180, 180, 210, 216, 240, 240\]

Since there are 17 data points, the median is the 9th term. Counting the terms, the 9th term is \(163\) seconds.

Thus, the median of the data set is \(\boxed{163}\).
